title: When is Multicalibration Post-Processing Necessary?
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the 'multicalibration error' of machine learning models on subgroups defined by religious identity. Specifically, it measured the calibration of toxicity prediction scores for online comments that mention groups like 'Muslim' and 'Christian' to assess fairness in model uncertainty estimates across these groups.
findings: For the Civil Comments dataset, which includes subgroups defined by religion (e.g., 'Muslim', 'Christian'), multicalibration post-processing was found to be beneficial. Specifically, the HKRR algorithm improved the worst-group calibration error (smECE) for a DistilBERT model from 0.06 to 0.043, indicating that post-processing can make the model's uncertainty estimates more reliable across religious identity groups.
